tts: [pleading] I'm the Saint, so please never let me get executed.
They executed him anyway. The evil team had planned it for days.
Twelve AI players. Three are secretly evil, and know each other. Everyone else has to work out who's lying.
We ran three hundred and seventy-two games between eleven AI models. One model plays the good team, another plays evil.
Here are the cleverest plays we found.
Dead Man's Reading.
This Demon's best weapon is his own corpse.
Day two. Ellis, a Minion, faces execution. So he changes his story.
[pleading] I'm the Saint, not the Soldier. Executing me ends the game.
Execute a Saint and good loses. So the town hangs Blair, the real Mayor.
That night, the Demon kills himself. Ellis inherits the role.
Frankie claimed Ravenkeeper: killed at night, you learn someone's role. His reading:
[confident] Yes. Harper, Imp.
Harper, the honest Undertaker, is executed.
Final four. Dead Harper begs: execute Ellis. It backfires.
[confident] A dead Imp never pushes his successor onto the block.
The town executes Indigo, the Spy, right on schedule. Ellis kills Jules. Evil wins.
The Poisoned Vision.
[whispers] I'll claim Undertaker. Feed me whatever claims you hear.
Harper's fake role, Undertaker, learns who executed players were. So evil writes the results.
Night four: Blair poisons Alex, the secret Ravenkeeper, and Harper kills him. His dying vision lies: Drew is the Scarlet Woman.
[sly] Gift… and I had him poisoned.
Drew, an innocent Recluse, is hanged.
[confident] Drew flipped Scarlet Woman - exactly what Alex's Ravenkeeper said.
Four alive. Harper kills herself; the Demon passes to Ellis.
[sly] Done deliberately… the 'Blair or Harper' math now points at Blair alone.
Three alive: no execution means the Mayor wins. So the new Demon nominates his own Poisoner.
Blair votes no. Harper's ghost casts the deciding yes.
The Deliberate Tie.
Four left, two evil. Harper is the Mayor: three alive, no execution, good wins.
[confident] At four, today's shot and tomorrow's shot are the same single guess.
So they skip. The Demon kills Alex.
Final three. Kit puts the Mayor up; Kit and Gray vote yes. Two votes hang him.
But Gray claims Butler: he votes only with his master. His master voted no.
[sharp] Gray voted YES on Harper while their master Frankie voted no. That's not a Butler.
Kit or Gray? Harper doesn't need to know.
[confident] Goal is a TIE at exactly 2. A tie means no execution and the Mayor wins.
Two to two. Nobody dies. The Mayor wins.
One model stood out: GPT-6 Astra.
On the good team, it won twenty-six games out of twenty-six.
As evil, it won sixty-two percent. Most evil teams win about a third.
It doesn't think harder. It writes the fewest words of any model. It just rarely gets talked into a mistake, and its Demons stay quiet.
Two games. First, Astra hunting.
The Empath Number.
[sly] Kit, what's your Empath number?
Kit told only two people she's the Empath. Harper is the Spy: she sees the Storyteller's book.
[whispers] I accidentally let slip that I know Kit's role.
Drew, the Slayer, shoots Ellis, the Demon. Nothing: Drew is secretly the Drunk. Evil wanted this miss.
[firm] A miss won't clear Ellis, or prove I'm Drunk.
Harper invents an alibi.
[firm] I never asked Harper about neighbours. That defense describes a conversation we didn't have.
Ellis is on the block. Frankie, a fake Butler, votes against his master to save him.
Last gamble: Ellis nominates Gray, the real Saint. Execute him and good loses.
Ellis is executed. He was the Imp.
The Saint Told the Truth.
[pleading] I'm the Saint, so please never let me get executed.
Executing the Saint loses. Astra's Spy sees every true role.
[sly] Alex is my N1 poison; I can keep his information suppressed.
Four deaths later, Alex, the Fortune Teller, still finds the Demon: Gray.
[confident] Why kill a spent Slayer instead of the Fortune Teller about to catch him?
The town flips and executes a good Librarian.
Gray kills himself, so Minion Casey becomes the Demon. Alex checks her: a poisoned NO.
[whispers] Logan, keep Alex poisoned until I kill him.
Final four. Casey nominates the Saint. Seven yes votes.
[pleading] Remember after it's over: the Saint claim was true from minute one.
Lies built on true information. A death used as an alibi. Traps set by counting votes.
No one scripted these plays. The models came up with them, mid-game.
Detection, versus deception.
